content:
Let the jagged line separating \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) have total length \(L\).

Let the parallelogram have side lengths \(a\) and \(b\), so opposite sides have equal lengths:
\[
AB=DC=a,\qquad AD=BC=b.
\]

Then
\[
\operatorname{Perimeter}(P_1)=L+AD+DC=L+b+a,
\]
while
\[
\operatorname{Perimeter}(P_2)=L+AB+BC=L+a+b.
\]

Thus the two parts have equal perimeters, regardless of the shape of their common boundary. Their areas, however, need not be equal.

\[
\boxed{\text{D: }P_1\text{ and }P_2\text{ have the same perimeter}}
\]
